packs.title: Meiji Shrine (Meiji Jingū), Shibuya, Tokyo — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Shinto shrine in a Shibuya forest, dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken. Precinct free of charge, sunrise to sunset; Inner Garden and Museum have fees.

packs.title: Meiji Jingū on foot from the Harajuku entrance — SanctaWay
packs.meta: A stop-by-step walk at Meiji Jingū from the Harajuku entrance along Minami-sandō to the main shrine, with the paid Inner Garden as the last stop.

packs.title: Meiji Shrine hours, admission and garden fees — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Precinct open sunrise to sunset with monthly clocks; free of charge. Inner Garden ¥500; Museum ¥1,000 / ¥900, 10:00–16:30, last admission 16:00, closed Thursdays.

packs.title: Meiji Shrine etiquette: photos, drones and food — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Preserve the dignity of this sacred place: no photos at the prayer line, no drones, no running or sports. Eat, drink and smoke only in designated areas.

packs.title: Meiji Shrine access: stations and walking times — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Harajuku and Meiji-jingumae: 1-minute walk to the entrance. Sangubashi 3 min; Yoyogi and Kita-sando 5. Then at least another ten minutes to the main shrine buildings.

packs.title: When to visit Meiji Shrine: seasons and hours — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Every season is worth a visit, official Q&A says. Recheck monthly sunrise and sunset hours; irises bloom in the Inner Garden in June, when garden hours extend.

packs.title: Meiji Shrine notes: check official pages first — SanctaWay
packs.meta: Recheck the official visit, garden, museum, access and etiquette pages before you go. Museum fees and Treasure Museum opening status are confirmed there.
